Inputs read: card #12967 (body, triage `6250766637`, claim `6251848893` as amended, os-dev-report `6252196216`), PR #12979 (body, 11 files, net diff), the head's 35 check-runs, and the `main` source the diff touches (read-only, for ①).

### ① Derived judgments

**Public-surface changes — the diff implies exactly two, both as claimed. Right.**
- `@object-ui/core`: the exported type `ParamCollectionHandler` (reached through `packages/core/src/actions/index.ts` → `export * from './ActionRunner.js'`) gains an optional third parameter `interpolate?: (text: string) => string`. Pure widening: TypeScript accepts an implementation with fewer parameters, so an existing handler that ignores the argument type-checks and behaves exactly as before (the runner still calls it with the same first two arguments; the third is ignored). The in-repo consumers that only forward the type (`packages/react/src/hooks/useActionRunner.ts`, `packages/react/src/context/ActionContext.tsx`) are untouched and still compile against the widened alias.
- `@object-ui/app-shell`: `ParamDialogState` gains an optional `interpolate` member. `ActionParamDialog` / `ParamDialogState` are not exported from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`, so this is not a public-surface change of the published package.
- `templateEvaluatorFor` is `private` on `ActionRunner`; `fillHoles` in `ActionParamDialog.tsx` is a module-local function; no other export moves. The `ActionDef.params` read is typed `Record<string, any>` already, so no type widens there. Right.

**The binding point.** `templateEvaluatorFor(action)` reads `action.params._rowRecord` (object, non-array) and returns `new ExpressionEvaluator({ ...this.context, record: row })`; otherwise the runner's own evaluator. `this.context` is already `withIdentityAlias`-ed at construction and on every `updateContext`, so the spread carries the identity aliases; the runner's evaluator is constructed from context alone (no shared formulas or cache the fresh instance would lack). The runner's `this.context` / `this.evaluator` are not mutated. It is evaluated once per `execute`, after the `condition` / `disabled` gates and before the confirm, and the same instance feeds both `confirmText` and the `interpolate` closure handed to the param handler, so confirm copy and dialog copy read one scope. Every row surface in the repo stashes the row under `params._rowRecord` and fires through `ActionRunner.execute` (`ObjectGrid.onActionDef`, `RelatedRecordActionsBridge.runRowAction`, `DeclaredActionsBar`, `containers.tsx` `dispatchHeaderAction`, `action-button.tsx` `withUndoBaseline`), and `execute` is the one place `confirmText` is evaluated — so the runner is the narrowest shared point; a grid-side fix would have left the related-list door raw. Right.

**Row wins over a page record.** `{ ...this.context, record: row }` overrides a page-level `record` only when a row is stashed. The three page-record stashes (`DeclaredActionsBar`, `containers.tsx` page header, `action-button.tsx` update write) stash the same record the page context carries, so nothing changes there. Right.

**Param dialog ordering.** `useConsoleActionRuntime`: `localizedDescription = actionDescription(...)` → `interpolate(localizedDescription)` → only then `[overrideNotice, declaredDescription].join('\n\n')`; the notice is concatenated verbatim, never evaluated (pinned by the new `overrideNotice` test case whose notice text contains a `${record.*}` spelling and survives untouched). `RecordDetailView`: `actionDescription(...)` then `interpolate(...)`; it has no override notice. `ActionParamDialog`: `fillHoles(pickLocalized(rawParam.helpText, language), state.interpolate)` — after the per-locale map is picked, so the hole is filled on the string the user reads; `fillHoles` only touches strings. `interpolate` is undefined-guarded on all three paths, so a third-party runner that supplies none prints as authored (CONTROL pins on each). Right.

**`RelatedRecordActionsBridge` — the one behaviour change, weighed.** The bridge runs inside `RecordDetailView`'s `ActionProvider`, whose context binds the PARENT page record; it already retargets the dispatch to the child (`objectName: childObject`, `recordId`, `params: { _rowRecord: record }`), and the api handler resolves the record id from that stash. Before this PR a `${record.*}` hole in a related-list row action's `confirmText` read the parent; now it reads the child row. That is the card's rule verbatim ("the record the action runs against is `record`"): the action runs against the child, and a confirm naming the parent while deleting the child was the mis-binding, not a feature. Search for a realistic reliant author: no `${record.*}` inside any `confirmText` / `description` / `helpText` anywhere in `examples/`, `apps/`, `content/docs`, package READMEs, demos or `.changeset/` (the only `${record.*}` uses in-repo are predicates, `params.recordId`, and `properties` on record surfaces); the bridge's own docblock promises nothing about `record`; cloud's consumer guard (cloud#3019) keeps `${record.*}` confirms header-only. No reliant author found. Judged right, and the "row wins over a page `record`" pin names the related-list case explicitly.

**Missing-field degradation.** The evaluator's template-part path returns `String(result ?? '')` for a member that reads `undefined`, so `${record.no_such_field}` prints empty on the header (measured in pin (c): `Pause ?`). A row dispatch now binds `record` and degrades identically; an UNBOUND root (`record` absent and no row) faults in `SafeExpressionParser` and returns the raw match, which is the pre-existing answer and stays (CONTROL: no-row dispatch unchanged). The card's control ("degrades the same way on both doors") is met. Right.

**Toasts.** The success/error toast reads `${result.*}` from the handler result on an unchanged path; pin (d) drives it through a row dispatch. Unchanged. Right.

**Bulk path.** `ObjectGrid`'s `stripCollectedActionKeys` removes `confirmText` / `confirm` / `params` / `actionParams` before the per-record dispatch, so the new binding never reaches it; `BulkActionDialog` prints its own multi-row confirm (noted by the dev, out of scope, no single record to bind). Right.

**Scope note, not a defect.** `condition`, `disabled`, the url target and `redirect` still read `this.evaluator`. The card's acceptance names `confirmText` and the dialog copy; row-level `condition` / `disabled` are already decided per row by the grid's row predicate before dispatch. Held to the ruled scope; no finding.

**Tests.** The core pin drives the SAME action through a header-shaped runner and a list-shaped runner with the exact `ObjectGrid` stash; the grid pin goes through the real row menu under a record-less provider; the dialog pin renders the real `ActionParamDialog`. Each positive has a CONTROL. The `paramRuntimeParity-6431` `DIALOG_READS` update is the right shape (both producers now write `interpolate`, parity still reads a declared list). Ablation reported on the one load-bearing line, 6 of 8 red, restore proven by blob. Not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/12967-row-action-record-hole.md`: `@object-ui/core: minor`, `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the correct arm: an exported type gained an optional parameter. Per the objectstack AGENTS.md rule, `yes` takes at least `minor` — core `minor` matches, and no `major` is declared (objectui AGENTS.md: breaking is spelled `minor` in this fixed group; `Changeset Bump Policy` check: success).
- app-shell `patch`: a bug fix in a released package with no barrel export change (`ParamDialogState` is internal) — `patch` is the floor the policy names for a fix and the right level.
- `plugin-grid` is touched by a test file only (`src/__tests__/…`), which publishes nothing; the presence gate asks for one declaration and `Changeset Declaration` / `Changeset Fixed Group Check` / `Changeset Claim Re-read` / `Changeset Overwrite Report` are all success on this head.
- The PR body and the claim both read `Clause-②: yes`; the changeset body states the widening and that a handler ignoring the argument reads as before. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation 1 (Clause-② measured `yes` against the claim's original `no`): answered — the claim was amended in place (`6251848893`, "amended in place from `no` on the dev's measurement"), the changeset carries `minor`, and this review is the one owed.
- Deviation 2 (three existing app-shell test files edited beyond the named surface): answered — two gained handler cases for the new argument and one parity list gained the new state key; no production file outside the claimed surface moved (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` and `RecordDetailView.tsx` are the param dialog's two state producers, within "the param dialog that prints those strings").
- Deviation 3 (no declaration-time refusal): answered on the merits — the card's refusal is conditional ("if a hole cannot be filled on some door"), and both doors now fill, so the condition is not met. The report cites "ruling 1" for this; no comment on the card is numbered as such, so the citation does not resolve, but the omission stands on the card's own wording. Not escalated.
- Out-of-scope finding (`BulkActionDialog` prints `def.confirmText` raw for a multi-row selection): correctly left unfiled as an observation — there is no single record for the rule to bind.
- Gate verdicts on the head at review time: success — Lint, Build & E2E, Test (dist pins), Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Declaration, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Overwrite Report, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Line Citation Gate, Live E2E (informational), label.
